column1: # The DUPLICATION DOCKET — one row per tag that two or more production files claim.
# Written by hand; `python3 tools/citations.py dups` reads it, and `dups --check`
# (in `make fast`) fails on a row that has none.
# ⚠ A ROW HERE IS A QUESTION THAT HAS BEEN ANSWERED, NOT A DEFECT.  Two files citing
# one rule may be one algorithm written twice — or one CONSTRAINT binding both, or two
# halves of a split the rule itself describes.  The verdict says which, with the
# argument, so nobody re-derives it next session.
# ⚠ AND THE FILE COUNT IS PART OF THE VERDICT.  A verdict is about the sites that were
# READ; when a new file claims the rule, the count no longer matches and the row goes
# back on the docket.  That is what makes "this becomes a duplicate at three" a
#   one         a genuine duplicate implementation — an open debt, merge it
#   merged      it was `one`; the merge has landed
#   broad       the RULE is too broad — the two sites are different things, sharpen it upstream
#   constraint  the tag names a rule that BINDS many sites, not an algorithm implemented once
#   inherent    really two, and the difference belongs to the application

column4: Thickness is palette-side, so a cell stores an id. That binds the palette reader, the selection, the wire, the plan's stroke, the octagon body and the field — six sites obeying one constraint, none of them an algorithm.
An opening is never absence. It binds the gesture that makes one, the session that picks its material, the mesher that draws it and the wire message — four obligations, one rule.
No odd multiple of 15 degrees exists. One library site obeys it; probe/h1 MEASURES it, which is the validation the rule asks for, not a second implementation.

⚠ WATCHED. A corner edge is claimed exactly once. `gesture.loft` ENFORCES one half of it — `wall_corner_close` writes the edge two runs both missed — and probe/b4y MEASURES the breach in both directions AND keeps the refuted other half, dropping the edge two runs both claim, as the control that says why only one half shipped. A probe calling the library function could only ever measure the variant that was chosen. If the drop is ever settled for good, the probe should call `wall_corner_close` and this row becomes `one`.
`WS_CONCURRENT` is declared once in hex_voxel; editor_server is its one consumer, discussing the case it names.
The authoring residual bound. session obeys it, probe/m1p measures it.
One upstream fact — the in-between period is 6.245 wu — justifying two independent choices: the reach's UNIT in session, and why the aim refusal is reachable in hex_editor. Neither computes it.
The agreement law binds `aim` and `run` and forbids mixing them in one gesture; probe/m2p measures the agreement. Four obligations plus its measurement.

There is no square sublattice of a hexagonal lattice, so a lattice polygon cannot be a rectangle. A FACT that binds, cited at three places that obey it and none that derive it: hex_editor where the footprint must not assume one; probe/pc as the measured explanation for `house_recover` refusing all 18 promoted floors; and probe/b5 as the reason the recovered room's hull is 5 or 6 vertices rather than 4 — *four walls* asks for a shape the lattice does not have. ⚠ Re-opened at three carriers 2026-08-29 and re-argued, which is what the file-count rule is for.

The rule describes a SPLIT — the cell carries an id, the palette carries the float — so both halves cite it. `moros_map/src/palette.loft` says so in its own words: "`@HB-X12` is the rule; this file is the other half of it."

Two DRIVERS of one gesture, verified rather than assumed: `editor_run` and `editor_server` both reach `press_verb` -> `tower_ring`, and `hex_shape::arc_fill` is called only in gesture.loft. The prose is near-identical; the code is one body.

A FACT that binds: no library derives the 1.1021 degree bias, they cite it — session for the gate's walk, gesture twice (the D conversion, and promote-on-close's reason that linework need not meet a corner), hex_editor at the call site. probe/h1 measures whether the bias is UNIFORM and probe/m1p what authoring RESOLUTION follows; those are its validation, not a second implementation.

A convex form's description is recovered from its CELLS, exactly and constructively. Cited at the primitive that acts on it (`promote_close` — why a closed loop must gain a floor), at its call site in `press_verb`, and at probe/b5, which MEASURES it: 25 of 25 rooms answer R1 with rho 0 for zero `run_edges`. ⛔ None of the three implements it — the implementation is `hex_recover::rebuild_construct`, upstream, which is the whole point of the row. ⚠ Re-opened at three carriers 2026-08-29.

⚠ WATCHED. One doorstep contract (ordinal offers, nominal refuses without one) carried by two structs — `hex_editor::Fit` and `hex_part::SocketFit` — which differ because each package answers in its own shape (a sentence plus ok, versus a code). A shared type needs a package below both, and the name `Fit` has already collided across this graph. A THIRD carrier makes this `one`.
